discovery: Theory of topological order and long-range entanglement in quantum matter
subfield: Condensed matter theory / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Wen and Kitaev showed that quantum phases of matter can be organized by patterns of long-range entanglement, not only by broken symmetry. Wen introduced topological order: ground-state degeneracy that depends on topology, fractionalized excitations and emergent gauge fields in fractional quantum Hall states and spin liquids. Kitaev's toric code and honeycomb model gave exactly solvable realizations with anyons and Majorana modes, and launched topologically protected quantum computation. Together with the Kitaev–Preskill and Levin–Wen topological entanglement entropy, their work turned entanglement into a diagnostic of quantum phases. These ideas now guide experiments on fractional Chern insulators in moire materials, Kitaev-candidate magnets, and the topological codes now built on superconducting and atomic quantum processors. Their framework goes beyond Landau's paradigm and now underpins condensed matter physics and quantum information science alike.
